correctness.rationale: Exact diagonal-plus-rank-one determinant lemma yields scalar secular inequality \(H_w(\Lambda)\le1\), equality iff the allocation support uses only maximizing affine candidates. Perron-Frobenius plus the diagonal boundary handles reducible matrices. The upper envelope of n affine lines has at most \(n-1\) genuine switches, and the explicit \(\delta=1/(8n^2)\) family proves sharpness with monotone rates. Independent fraction arithmetic of seven three-class allocations across five q and all \(2\le n\le16\) reproduces each certificate; finite testing is not used as proof.

originality.rationale: A motivated, exact all class counts and all-frequency simplex optimizer/support classification with a sharp biologically ordered switching construction was not found among the named inspected sources or actual targeted record queries. Qualitative depth reversals and general Perron/rank-one spectral techniques are known and excluded from novelty. The Eager et al. 2013 full text remained inaccessible, and an implicit stronger classical result remains possible; this is best-knowledge same-model originality, not independent priority certification.
residual_risks: Complete original Eager et al. 2013 depth-disturbance paper could not be read despite repository and author-copy attempts, so a hidden special-case equality/switch theorem could have been missed.
Classical rank-one matrix extremization may imply a narrower pure-allocation corollary without the exact present ecological packaging; full novelty depends on precise theorem comparison.
Semantic record indexing and accessible full-text corpus are incomplete.
Published stochastic population measures differ from expectation; extrapolating the result to realistic persistence would be wrong.

value.rationale: Seed placement balances high dormant survival against high disturbance-driven germination, a biologically meaningful policy allocation. The result gives every optimal mixture, every frequency interval and a sharp all class counts switch ceiling, plus constructions respecting ordered depth-survival/germination tradeoffs. This is a natural complete classification rather than an arbitrary numerical case, while its expected-growth objective is explicitly narrower than stochastic persistence.
